question: What is the typical age range generally used to define adolescence?
explanation: Adolescence is widely defined by health organizations as the transitional period from childhood to adulthood occurring between ages 10 and 19. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why do nurses divide adolescence into different stages?

options.A: It removes the need to talk directly to the patient
options.B: It proves that teenagers will always rebel against authority
options.C: It helps identify normal milestones versus clinical problems
options.D: It stops physical growth from happening too quickly

explanation: Spot on! Breaking adolescence down into stages helps you anticipate what changes are normal and catch any health or developmental delays early. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the typical age range for early adolescence?
explanation: Early adolescence generally covers the ages of 10 to 13, marked heavily by the onset of puberty. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why do young teens sometimes look a bit clumsy or awkward?

options.A: The brain shrinks temporarily during a growth spurt
options.B: Bones grow faster than the supporting muscles and tendons
options.C: Vision blurs due to rapid eyeball enlargement
options.D: Inner ear fluid production increases rapidly

explanation: Correct! Their bones shoot up faster than their muscles can keep up with, which temporarily throws off their balance and coordination. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h2)

question: What type of thinking skills usually show up during middle adolescence?
explanation: Well done! Middle adolescents start thinking beyond what's right in front of them—they can grasp abstract ideas and imagine 'what if' scenarios. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why do middle adolescents often take big risks even when they know the rules?

options.A: They lack the physical capacity to understand danger
options.B: Peer pressure is the only cause of adolescent accidents
options.C: The emotional brain matures faster than the impulse-control brain center
options.D: Their long-term memory is completely deactivated

explanation: You got it! The emotional part of the brain develops faster than the part that controls impulses, making them crave exciting rewards while struggling to put on the brakes. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is a major mental and emotional milestone in late adolescence?

options.A: Total dependence on parental rule enforcement
options.B: Consolidation of a stable personal identity
options.C: Complete mastery of concrete physical skills
options.D: The initial onset of secondary sex characteristics

explanation: Spot on! By late adolescence, kids are figuring out who they truly are, what they value, and where they are headed in life. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h4)

question: How do friendships usually shift as a teen moves from middle to late adolescence?

options.A: Social interactions stop happening outside of school
options.B: Friends become completely unimportant to the individual
options.C: Peer group pressure decreases as personal independence grows

explanation: Correct! While friends are everything in middle adolescence, older teens get more comfortable standing on their own two feet and trusting their own choices. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h4)

question: What does the letter 'D' stand for in the HEADSS adolescent assessment tool?
explanation: In the HEADSS screening tool, 'D' stands for drugs, alcohol, and tobacco use habits. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is it a good idea for a nurse to spend part of a teen's visit talking to them alone?

options.A: To prevent the teenager from asking medical questions
options.B: To save time during a busy hospital shift
options.C: To encourage honest answers about sensitive topics like sex and drugs
options.D: To prove to the parents that they are no longer needed in the room

explanation: Spot on! Teens open up much more honestly about sensitive topics when they know their parents aren't sitting right there listening. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which mental health challenges most commonly first appear during the teenage years?
explanation: Well done! Because of all the massive body changes and social stress, depression and anxiety often peak or first show up during these years. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to approach health promotion with teenagers?

options.A: Ignoring lifestyle habits until adulthood is reached
options.B: Reporting all experimental behavior to the local police
options.C: Using strict scare tactics to prevent bad habits
options.D: Providing non-judgmental guidance and open education

explanation: You got it! Teens respond best when we listen without scolding them, offering honest education and support they can trust. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h6)
